known_information: The report identifies auto-updated0.102.3001, Windows10 22H2/build19045.7807, per-user installation and elevated execution. New key and Use Service both fail despite restarting.
Both supplied screenshots were inspected: the pairing banner and the service-mode-change error agree with the reported transitions; no pairing secret is displayed.

Downloaded and inspected the supplied diagnostic ZIP, including the complete Settings log and both MWB logs. The Settings log contains18121 untrusted-signature occurrences and17 pairing-update failures.

The Settings log explicitly reports Rejected SettingsSync server: untrusted-signature during GetSettingsSyncHelperAsync and Mouse Without Borders shutdown endpoint is unavailable during the service transition.

In the exact released code, ConnectSettingsSyncHelperAsync verifies the local server before creating SyncHelper. SubmitNewKeyRequestAsync and SubmitShutdownRequestAsync depend on that endpoint. A verification rejection can therefore explain these two UI failures without first diagnosing the remote network.

Existing open issue50795 tracks the same signature rejection, including confirmed0.102.3001 reports. Its precise certificate-mismatch subtype is corroborated by other installations, not independently measured from this report ZIP.
Read complete body, empty discussion, label-only timeline and existing fork traces; no competing design or linked implementation was found.

title: The unlimited-range mouse is not functioning properly.

comment.body: Thanks for attaching the diagnostic ZIP and screenshots. I inspected the logs: Settings repeatedly reports `Rejected SettingsSync server: untrusted-signature`; it also reports that the MWB shutdown endpoint is unavailable when changing service mode. In 0.102.3001, New key and the service transition both depend on that verified local Settings-to-MWB connection, so the two failures are consistent with the signing/verification problem tracked in #50795. Please consolidate this report with that issue and keep the existing diagnostic attachment; another generic log collection or restart is not the next useful step. The logs prove the rejection class, not the exact signer-certificate mismatch on this individual machine. No signature bypass, manual key copying, or network reconfiguration is recommended. The tracking issue remains open; a released repair is not being claimed.
